value: NONE EXISTS (no published orbital quantity comparable to the Earth quartz index)
product_or_paper: Tarnas et al. 2019 GRL 46:12771 (hydrated silica, CRISM); Salvatore et al. 2018 Icarus 301:76 (TIR bulk mineralogy); Ninomiya et al. 2005 RSE 99 (QI)
quoted_evidence: Tarnas abstract: 'We detected hydrated silica in Jezero crater'. Brown news: 'we found two outcrops of hydrated silica within Jezero crater'. arXiv 1107.3499: 'emissivity is higher at ASTER band 11 than at bands 10 and 12'; QI 'expected to be high for quartzite and other siliceous rocks'. Salvatore abstract: region dominated by basaltic compositions.
definition: Earth QI = Band11 x Band11 / (Band10 x Band12) on ASTER 8.125-9.275 um bands; the equation text was lost in the arXiv PDF extraction I opened, the formula was seen in a search excerpt and the arXiv page credits Ninomiya et al. 2005 (RSE vol 99). Mars results are CRISM near-infrared detections of hydrated silica at two outcrops (no abundance or index value) and TIR deconvolution at kilometre scale (no silica number for Jezero in the abstract).
pixel_size: CRISM pixel size not stated in the text I opened; TES footprint about 3 x 6 km (Meteoritics and Planetary Science 38:871)
comparability_to_earth: NOT COMPARABLE: Earth QI measures crystalline quartz via an 8-9 um emissivity contrast at 100 m; Mars has only presence detections of hydrated (opaline) silica and basaltic bulk compositions
status: UNVERIFIED (formula and Ninomiya 2005 credit VERIFIED from opened pages; absence of a Jezero silica number is 'none found' not proof)

product_or_paper: SWIM 2.0 Combined Ice Consistency (Morgan et al. 2021 Nature Astronomy 5:230); SWIM project
quoted_evidence: SWIM LPSC 2019 abstract: ice mapped 'from 0 to 60 N in four longitude bands' including Utopia 70-150 E. SWIM 2.0 page: 'Pixel scale = 3000 m', 'Latitude = -60 - 60N', 'No data = -30'.
definition: Composite ice consistency map by depth range (0-1 m, 1-5 m, >5 m) from neutron, thermal, radar and geomorphology data. Jezero (18.4 N, 77.5 E) lies inside the stated 0-60 N and 70-150 E bounds by my reading, but I did not open a GeoTIFF or read a value there. The SWIM 1.0 page says low-latitude areas without observed glacial or periglacial features get a negative geomorphology value, so a low or negative value is plausible but unconfirmed.
comparability_to_earth: NOT COMPARABLE: our Earth water_index is an aridity index (decided); SWIM is a subsurface ice likelihood
status: UNVERIFIED (product and coverage VERIFIED; value at Jezero not read)

product_or_paper: MGS TES Dust Cover Index, Ruff and Christensen 2002 JGR 107 (doi 10.1029/2001JE001580)
quoted_evidence: ASU DCI page: map shows 'average emissivity from 1350 to 1400 cm-1' where lower emissivity means fine dust. ASU data page: 16 ppd, 3.5 km per pixel, 5760x2880.
definition: Surface fine-silicate dust cover index, independent of albedo and thermal inertia; spectra with water-ice opacity above 0.07 or dust opacity above 0.29 are excluded. The ASU product page and dci.html would not open by fetch (redirect not followed, and dci.html is not on the allowlist); numbers come from search excerpts of those pages. No Jezero value and no raster download link or file size found.
comparability_to_earth: NOT COMPARABLE: our Earth dust_index is atmospheric (MERRA-2 dust or MODIS aerosol); DCI is surface dust cover
